_comment: OWNER 2026-08-13/14, asked directly: 'draw over the hero AND be passable.' town.html paints one flat baked painting and then sorts NPCs/hero by foot Y on top of it, so nothing in the painting can ever draw in FRONT of her -- she always appears to stand on whatever tall thing she is actually standing under or behind. scripts/derive_town_foreground.py extracts the pixels listed here from the SAME locked painting (design/act1-towns/portSapphire-screen-v5-graded.png == the shipped public/act1-hifi/town/portSapphire-screen.png, byte-identical) into public/act1-hifi/town/portSapphire-foreground.png, a transparent layer town.html now draws AFTER the hero/NPC sort. The base painting is never touched -- see the script's own hash check.
_extraction: Within each region's bboxArt, a pixel is kept OPAQUE if it fails the same paving_mask() test scripts/derive_town_walkable.py uses for collision (i.e. it reads as something other than pale cobblestone -- wood, metal, glass, stone, roof tile, foliage), and made transparent otherwise, so real pavement gaps between chain links or under a roof eave stay see-through. This is the same colour test the collision authority already trusts, applied to a different question: not 'can she stand here' but 'is this pixel part of the overhead prop, not the ground behind it'.
_removedProps: OWNER 2026-08-15, verbatim: 'the chimny issue is not being fixed correctly ... there is an easier fix though: just remove the chimnys and demijohn so there is not confusion where players can walk.' The chimney-tower and demijohn regions that used to live here are GONE -- scripts/apply_removal (run once, not repo-tracked) clone-patched both out of the locked painting itself, sampling nearby cobble, and the pixel diff against the prior committed painting is confined to exactly their two bboxes (proof: design/act1-towns/portSapphire-foreground-proof.png regenerated below shows only ship-mast opaque now). The ship's mast stays -- OWNER 2026-08-03, unambiguous, not part of this change.

regions.why: Same object as the collision exemption of the same id in portSapphire-authored-obstacles.json (centerArt [900,1256] r=30) -- confirmed member. The bbox is wider than the exemption circle because the visible rigging/stays fan out further than the small collision-relevant disk at deck level; occlusion is a purely visual question, not a collision one, so it does not need to match the circle.
